$comment: Golden vectors for ONE question: how is the model id a transcript recorded SHOWN, and which FAMILY does it count under?
The round card reads `written with Opus 5.5 (main) · 3 Sonnet coders · …`; the report E6 builds counts the same coders by the
same family. Two implementations of one rule drift, so both answer THIS file (`authorsLine.test.ts` for the extension; E6's C#
family function reads it too — never a retyped copy).
The rule: `claude-<family>-<major>-<minor>[-<date>]` — <family> lower-case letters, <major> digits, <minor> one or two digits, an
optional eight-digit date — is shown as `<Family> <major>.<minor>` and its family is `<family>`. An empty model, and the word
`unknown` (E4.S3's launch-only row), are family `unknown`. ANY other id is shown verbatim and counts as family `other`: a new
naming scheme is never guessed into a family it may not belong to, and a `[1m]` suffix is part of the id the transcript wrote.
The page escapes what it shows; the vectors carry the text as it arrives, hostile ones included.
